body.x: AVING News selected ▲uSens’ “Impression PI”, ▲IONVR’s “IONVR”, ▲Creative’s “Blaster X VR”, ▲Skully’s “SKULLY AR-1”, and ▲Royole’s “Royole-X” as the top five products among gaming, VR, and AR fields, which were showcased at “CES (Consumer Technology Show) 2016”, the world’s largest IT consumer electronics exhibition. It ran for four days from Wednesday the 6th to Saturday the 9th in Las Vegas.

This product integrates AR and VR. Able to be connected to mobile devices, users can use smartphones such as iPhone 6 and Galaxy Gear as screens. Users can change video contents or answer phone calls without taking it off.

This is a VR headset that can be applied to smartphones with various sizes -- from 4.5 to 6 inches. By using MotionSync technology, which provides a hardware-based solution to reduce motion blurring, users can experience smooth, high-quality mobile virtual reality.

"Blaster X VR" is a VR device for smartphones, and it is particularly great for watching videos shared on Blaster Zone. Blaster Zone is a video recording and sharing service that Creative newly launched. If users install the company’s own recording APK and record videos, they can watch 360-degree videos from whatever angle they choose.

“SKULLY AR-1”, a smart motorcycle helmet, is connected to a smartphone and shows a variety of information. It features a built-in 180-degree Blindspot Camera, installed for unparalleled situational awareness and safety, and a head-up display. It looks every second in 360 degrees, and focuses ahead of roads.

This product is a smart mobile theater. Unlike existing 3D VR products, where they must be inserted into smartphones, “Royole-X” possesses its own screen and audio equipment. Users can connect it to their smartphones and watch movies. In particular, it focuses on its theater concept and image and sound quality. It supports HDMI, wireless Wi-Fi, and external hard drives. With its 6000mAh battery, it can run for about five hours.

“CES”, which is held every year in January by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is the world’s largest IT consumer electronics exhibition, showcasing global trends in the electronics and IT industry. AVING News, which has sent reporters to CES for 11 years, will introduce various up-to-date technologies and products showcased at CES 2016. Based on keen reports and research at CES, AVING News will hold the “CES 2016 Review Conference” at Korea AVING Studio on Wednesday the 28th.→ Go to 'CES 2016' news page
